The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are set to be unveiled next week, and a new report has shed more light on the flagship phones' "mechanical aperture" camera feature, as well as mentioning an improved vapor chamber and other configurations.

Below are the new features of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max as revealed by Mark Gurman

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman published his latest predictions today regarding the new iPhones set to launch on September 9.

Although most of the report covers features that have already been reported, there are a few noteworthy details.

For example, Apple will bring a brand-new "mechanical aperture" camera feature to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, with the smaller iPhone 18 Pro also likely to feature it.

Although this camera upgrade has been reported numerous times and is also known as a "variable aperture," there has been little detail on what it can actually do. However, Gurman reported today that the feature is used to "fine-tune light and depth-of-field control."

In addition, a new report also mentioned that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will feature "longer battery life and an improved vapor chamber to prevent overheating."

Improved battery life was already expected, so having it confirmed is certainly good news. However, the mention of an improved vapor chamber is new information.

Apple first adopted a vapor chamber design in the iPhone 17 Pro last year, and it appears the company is now ready to roll out a second-generation version.

Finally, Gurman stated that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be equipped with "its in-house C2 modem chip." Although this is not a new rumor, it is worth mentioning, as some reports had indicated that Apple would continue to use Qualcomm's modem chips this year.

To find out what else to expect from the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, check out our related reports.
